title: Independent evaluation finds Google Flood Hub and GloFAS forecasts skillful beyond four days in Mali's frequently flooded regions, suggesting seven-day Red Cross early-action triggers
summary: Independent study finds Google Flood Hub skillful beyond 4-day lead time, enough for 7-day Mali Red Cross early action triggers.
account: A peer-reviewed study in the Journal of Flood Risk Management evaluated Google Flood Hub (GFH), Google's AI-based flood forecasting service. It was published online 16 September 2026, in volume 19, issue 3, September 2026. The authors are researchers from the Netherlands Red Cross 510 data team and Utrecht University. They are also from the EU Joint Research Centre, Politecnico di Milano and the University of Twente. They compared GFH with GloFAS and the Mali Red Cross's existing Early Action Protocol trigger, using discharge observations and district-level impact data. The existing trigger relies on upstream water levels and is limited to a four-day lead time. The authors report that GloFAS and GFH demonstrate sufficient skill for early action beyond a four-day lead time in frequently flooded regions. They suggest early action plans could operate with a seven-day lead time and span a larger area. No realized early action is documented.
purpose: AI-based riverine flood forecasting for ungauged basins to support early warning and anticipatory action.
deployer: Evaluated for the Mali Red Cross Early Action Protocol; not documented as an operational trigger
taxonomy_note: A forecast-skill evaluation is read as task accuracy; no early action is documented.

ai_role.statement: The study evaluates GFH forecast skill directly against observations and impact data; it does not document any decision or action taken on a GFH forecast.
